one_liner: Google's AI notebook that summarizes and answers questions from user-uploaded sources and generates audio overviews/podcasts.
access_note: Consumer NotebookLM has no public API at all; the adjacent 'Gemini Notebook Enterprise' API requires a Google Cloud project, IAM roles, and paid enterprise licensing, still labeled Preview/Pre-GA.
api_breadth_note: Enterprise API only covers notebook CRUD plus source and audio-overview generation endpoints; no query/chat/answer endpoint documented.
existing_mcp_note: No MCP server specific to NotebookLM/Notebook Enterprise found.
main_blocker: Consumer NotebookLM is blocked (no API); the enterprise variant only works inside an org that already has a Google Cloud project and licenses.

evidence.note: Official REST reference for creating/managing notebooks; confirms gcloud-token auth and Preview status.
Google's own developer forum confirms there is no public API for consumer NotebookLM.

researcher_notes: The hint conflates two different products: consumer NotebookLM (no API) and 'Gemini Enterprise' (a gated Preview REST API).

one_liner: AI meeting transcription and notes tool that records, transcribes, and summarizes conversations.
access_note: There is no self-serve API key program ('we currently do not have a public API key at this time' per Otter's own help center); the only sanctioned programmatic path is the OAuth-authenticated MCP server.
api_breadth_note: The official MCP surface exposes only 3 tools: search meetings, fetch a transcript, and get user info — no write/create endpoints.
existing_mcp_note: Official Otter MCP Server, OAuth-authenticated, listed in Claude's and ChatGPT's official connector/app directories.
main_blocker: No generic API key/developer program; an agent toolkit can only be built against the official OAuth MCP server's 3 read-only tools.

evidence.note: Official help center article: full MCP setup instructions, tool list, and FAQ confirming no public API key exists yet.

researcher_notes: Community/unofficial repos exist reverse-engineering internal endpoints, but Otter explicitly does not support this for third parties.

one_liner: AI meeting recorder that produces transcripts, summaries, and action items from video calls.
access_note: Any user can generate an API key immediately from their own account settings with no sales contact or paid plan required; keys are scoped to the user's own/shared meetings.
api_breadth_note: Endpoints cover meetings, transcripts, summaries, action items, downloads, teams, users, webhooks, and a full OAuth2 app flow, plus official SDKs.
existing_mcp_note: Official Fathom MCP server with documented setup for Claude and ChatGPT, separate from an unofficial community MCP that also exists.

evidence.note: Confirms self-serve API key generation and working curl/Python/TS examples.
Full docs index confirming REST API, OAuth, webhooks, SDKs, and an official MCP section.

researcher_notes: One of the most agent-ready apps in this batch: free self-serve key, mature REST API, official SDKs, webhooks, official MCP.

one_liner: AI-powered search engine over 200M+ peer-reviewed academic papers that synthesizes evidence-based answers.
access_note: The raw 'Consensus API' is application-only with custom quoted pricing ($0.10/call + platform fee); by contrast the official MCP server is freely usable via OAuth with no account required for basic search.
api_breadth_note: Both the raw API and the MCP server expose essentially one capability — paper search — with filters like year, study type, and journal quality.
existing_mcp_note: Official Consensus MCP, supports Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Codex, VS Code, Windsurf via OAuth or bearer token.
main_blocker: The general-purpose REST API requires a sales application and custom quote; agents can practically only reach Consensus via the free/no-account OAuth MCP server, which has tighter limits.

evidence.note: Full MCP docs: server URL, OAuth flow, tool schema, access tiers.
Marketing/pricing page stating the API is 'available by application only.'

researcher_notes: Two very different access paths exist under the same brand — a nearly-free MCP server and a sales-gated raw API.

one_liner: Agentic document processing platform that parses, extracts, classifies, splits, and edits PDFs and other complex documents into structured data.
access_note: Self-serve signup grants 15,000 free credits before any billing is required; pay-as-you-go credits after that, with a separate paid Growth tier for enterprise features.
api_breadth_note: Distinct Classify, Parse, Extract, Split, and Edit APIs, composable Pipelines, plus SDKs and a CLI.
existing_mcp_note: Official Reducto MCP server, hosted and local modes, full tool reference (parse_document, extract_data, split_document, classify_document, edit_document, etc.).
researcher_notes: Very agent-ready: official MCP server even exposes a get_documentation tool for coding agents.

one_liner: Cognition's autonomous AI software engineer agent that can be spun up via API to plan, code, and complete engineering tasks end-to-end.
access_note: Generating a usable API key requires a paid Cognition/Devin account — the Team plan is explicitly marketed as including API access; no free self-serve API tier was found.
api_breadth_note: v3 API covers session creation/interaction/search, playbooks, knowledge base CRUD, schedules, integrations, and enterprise/org management.
existing_mcp_note: Official Devin MCP server, requiring a service-user or personal-access API key.
main_blocker: Requires a paid Devin/Cognition account before any key can be generated; no free trial API tier confirmed.

evidence.note: Official MCP docs: server URL, auth headers, full tool catalog.
Official auth docs explaining service-user keys vs personal access tokens.

researcher_notes: Pricing details came from third-party summary sites, not fetched directly from Cognition's own pricing page — worth confirming.

one_liner: AI creative suite for generating and editing images, video, audio, and 3D content across 30+ models, usable via CLI, MCP, or REST API.
access_note: Developers can self-serve create an API key at cloud.higgsfield.ai, and the CLI/MCP paths use a browser-based account login with no API key needed; generation is billed via Higgsfield's existing credit/plan system.
api_breadth_note: Async job-based endpoints for image/video/audio/3D generation, character training, and generation-history browsing across 30+ underlying models.
existing_mcp_note: Official Higgsfield MCP & CLI, works with Claude, OpenClaw, Hermes, and any MCP-compatible client.

evidence.note: Official CLI/MCP landing page: install command, browser-based auth login flow, FAQ confirming no API key needed for MCP/CLI.
Official CLI GitHub repo confirming npm install and auth login flow.

researcher_notes: Raw REST API pricing/free-tier terms should be double-checked; only found via search-result summaries.

one_liner: Open-source command-line tool (mmdc) that renders Mermaid diagram-definition files into SVG/PNG/PDF images, runnable locally or via Docker.
access_note: It's a free, MIT-licensed, open-source npm package that anyone can install and run locally with no account, key, or network call to a hosted service required.
api_breadth_note: Single function surface — convert a Mermaid definition to an image/PDF — exposed as CLI flags and a Node.js API; not a hosted network API at all.
existing_mcp_note: No MCP server confirmed by direct research; several community MCP servers for Mermaid rendering are known to exist in the broader ecosystem but none was independently confirmed here.

evidence.note: Official repo: install command, usage, Docker/Node.js API alternatives, MIT license.
npm package page confirming current published version.

researcher_notes: Pure local CLI/rendering tool, not a hosted API — an agent toolkit would just shell out to mmdc, no auth needed.

one_liner: Third-party REST API (transcriptapi.com, unaffiliated with YouTube/Google) that extracts YouTube video transcripts plus video/channel/playlist search data.
access_note: Signup grants 100 free credits with no card required, then paid plans start at $5/month; API key is generated instantly on signup with no approval step.
api_breadth_note: Endpoints for transcript extraction, YouTube-wide search, in-channel search, channel video listing, playlist extraction, and a free RSS-based 'latest uploads' endpoint.
existing_mcp_note: Official hosted MCP server, documented with Claude Code/Cursor/VS Code install snippets.

evidence.note: Primary marketing/docs page: free-credit signup, REST endpoint examples, MCP config snippets, pricing table.

researcher_notes: This is an unofficial third-party scraper/wrapper around YouTube's public caption surface (not the official YouTube Data API) — carries ToS/reliability risk despite being fully self-serve.

one_liner: AI meeting recording and note-taking platform (no-bot capture) with AI summaries, action items, and conversation intelligence.
access_note: Grain's own FAQ states plainly 'the Free plan does not include API access'; Personal Access Tokens require the paid Starter plan and above.
api_breadth_note: Endpoints cover listing/getting recordings and transcripts, uploading external recordings, tagging, sharing, webhooks, users, teams, and meeting types; supports personal and workspace tokens plus OAuth2.
existing_mcp_note: No dedicated Grain MCP server was found or confirmed; Grain's docs emphasize REST + webhooks, not MCP.
main_blocker: Requires at minimum a paid Starter-plan Grain subscription to generate any API token; the Free plan has zero API access.

evidence.note: Official support article: full auth model, rate limits, and explicit FAQ confirming Free plan excludes API access.
Confirms Free/Starter/Business/Enterprise tiers and that paid plans unlock API access.

researcher_notes: Solid, mature REST API once past the paywall — the only real blocker is that it's paid-plan-gated from the very first API call.
